Hi Martin —

Appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front, then next steps below: 

- Multi-entity offers: AWS Marketplace private offers are tied to a single payer/legal entity by default. For multi-entity buys we generally recommend either (a) a master buyer PO per legal entity staged in parallel, or (b) a delegated activation flow where you coordinate internal purchase orders and we activate them against the same seller offer. We can outline the activation steps for each path.

- Term lengths: Marketplace supports 12 and 24 month private offers natively. 36-months is possible but requires additional finance signoff and a non-standard commercial approval (we can route that internally).

- Evidence & VAT invoice: attaching an evidence pack and the latest price sheet. We can provide a sample VAT invoice once we know the buyer legal entity and region.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll loop in our Deals lead (Vivek) and Finance contact to confirm approval thresholds for >24 months.
2) If you prefer, share the buyer legal entity names (DE/FR/UK) and we’ll draft a recommended activation sequence (single PO per entity with suggested invoice language).
3) We’ll prepare a draft private-offer letter for your procurement team to attach to their PO.

Thanks for the ping. Short policy notes from Deals/Finance POV:

- Standard private-offer term support = 12 / 24 months.
- 36 months: allowed but requires a Finance commercial exception (approval from Director of Revenue Ops) and Legal review to ensure renewal/termination language aligns with Marketplace activation windows.
- Discount thresholds: anything >20% list requires approval from my org (Deals). If you need a multi-year price concession (e.g., larger discount for 36 months) include the proposed discount % in the submission.

Recommended execution:
1) Ask customer to confirm the three buyer legal entity names and projected ARR by entity.
2) If the customer wants a single commercial package across entities, structure as parallel private offers (one offer per legal entity) with identical terms and a coordinating appendix that we store off-marketplace — this keeps AWS activation simple and keeps legal/finance happy.
3) I’ll route a formal exception if they request 36 months and the discount is >15%.

I can take point on the internal approval once Hannah sends the ARR breakdown.

Hi all —

Quick confirmation from Finance/Operations side and a draft activation plan below. Happy to run a short call if useful.

VAT / Invoice notes:
- We issue VAT invoices per selling legal entity. For DE/FR/UK each country requires separate invoice headers and VAT registration numbers. We can provide sample invoices for each once you confirm the buyer entity legal names.
- UK buyers: post-Brexit, UK VAT handling differs; we may need the buyer’s UK VAT registration to avoid reverse-charge confusion.

Draft activation sequence (recommended):
1) Customer provides three PO PDFs (one per legal entity). Each PO references the same Redwood private-offer SKU and attaches the procurement letter we provide.
2) Customer sends a one-page master payment allocation memo (internal for their finance) that explains how spend is split across entities — this helps later audits.
3) Redwood creates equivalent private offers in AWS Marketplace for each seller/buyer pairing and attaches the corresponding invoice template to the deal.
4) If 36 months requested: proceed to step to request a Finance exception (Vivek will own the routing). Expect ~5 business days for internal approval plus Legal review.

Attachments: sample VAT invoice (placeholder in evidence pack), activation-checklist.docx (we can send after this thread).

Martin — happy to draft the procurement letter and sample invoices once you share the buyer legal names. If you’d like a short 20-minute sync to walk procurement through the activation steps, we can schedule early next week.
